I farm the way I know best: I keep cotton as my main crop because that is my usual system and it gives me the most dependable cash return on my land. I have only 9 mu and some family labor is away working off-farm, so I will keep the plan simple and manageable. I will put most of the land into cotton, then keep a smaller area in maize and mungbean so I still have grain and a low-cost legume in the year. Because I have well irrigation, I will use water to protect yield at key stages, but I will not over-irrigate because that adds cost. I will use improved seed where it helps me most, especially for cotton and maize, and I will keep fertilizer moderate and practical based on my experience. Cotton will get the highest input because it is my main income crop. Maize will get medium input for stable production. Mungbean will get the lightest input because it needs less fertilizer and helps me spread risk. I will use rotary tillage for convenience and labor saving on most fields, and I will keep pesticide sprays to the level I think is necessary rather than excessive.
